column1: Debiasing the Fine-Grained Classification Task in LLMs with Bias-Aware PEFT
note:
Core Problem (Layer-Wise Bias Propagation): The paper identifies two fine-grained label biases in LLMs: Prediction Propensity Bias (over-preference for high-frequency labels) and Discriminative Ability Bias (inability to distinguish low-frequency labels). It reveals that these biases stem from early prediction errors in intermediate layers and continuously accumulate toward deeper layers.

Methodological Innovation (Interchange Ablation & Layer Localization): Instead of modifying all layers, the authors apply Interchange Ablation (swapping the activations of gold samples with biased samples) and measure output KL divergence across layers. This pinpoints the exact single intermediate layer $\ell$ responsible for the strongest bias propagation.

The Proposed Strategy (Intermediate PEFT & Bias Balance Loss): The framework unfreezes less than 1% of total parameters—specifically targeting o_proj (attention output) and down_proj (MLP down-projection) in the target layer—while keeping the rest frozen. It introduces a dual Bias Balance Loss ($\mathcal{L}_{bal1} + \mathcal{L}_{bal2}$) to simultaneously equalize logit variance across labels and maximize the distance between target and non-target representations.

Strategic Advantage for ITTS (Surgical Mid-Layer Intervention): This layer-wise diagnostic and intervention strategy proves that bias can be cleanly intercepted mid-stream before it amplifies. For ITTS Text Encoders, it provides a blueprint for low-cost, layer-specific debiasing: rather than retraining the entire encoder or distorting global embeddings, one can apply minimal parameter edits at the exact layer where bias spikes, preserving the encoder’s ability to handle explicit stylistic or gender instructions.

column1: Towards Understanding Task-agnostic Debiasing Through the Lenses of Intrinsic Bias and Forgetfulness
note:
Core Contribution (The "Forgetfulness" Problem): The paper addresses a critical flaw in task-agnostic debiasing: Catastrophic Forgetting of Fairness. It reveals that pre-trained language models tend to "relearn" social biases when fine-tuned on downstream tasks, rendering initial debiasing efforts ineffective.

Methodological Innovation (CMA-Driven Regularization): Instead of full-parameter tuning or blind freezing, the authors utilize Causal Mediation Analysis (CMA) as an auditing mechanism. By measuring the indirect effects of specific attention heads, CMA precisely pinpoints which heads are successfully debiased and which are crucial for task generalization.

The Proposed Algorithm (ProSocialTuning): Based on the CMA findings, the algorithm applies a targeted Generalization-Guided Regularization. It acts as an "anchor," specifically penalizing changes to those critical, debiased attention heads during fine-tuning. This mathematically prevents the model from recovering its biased state while maintaining downstream performance.

Strategic Advantage for ITTS (Architectural Alignment): Since the framework is natively validated on BERT-base (Transformer Encoder architecture), its head-level intervention strategy is highly transferable to ITTS Text Encoders. It offers a blueprint for precision debiasing: selectively fixing the "biased heads" while preserving the encoder's ability to strictly follow explicit stylistic or gender-based instructions.

column1: LEACE: Perfect linear concept erasure in closed form
note:
Core Problem (Linear Concept Leakage & Over-Distortion): Sensitive attributes (e.g., gender, race) are easily detected by linear classifiers within pre-trained embeddings. Existing debiasing methods (like INLP or RLACE) either fail to achieve complete erasure or severely distort the overall feature space, harming downstream task capabilities.

Theoretical Innovation (Centroid Equivalence & Linear Guardedness): The authors prove a fundamental mathematical equivalence: a feature space achieves linear guardedness (where no linear classifier can predict the protected concept better than random/constant guessing) if and only if all concept classes share the exact same mean feature vector (centroid).

The Proposed Strategy (Closed-Form Optimal Affine Transformation): Based on this equivalence, the paper derives LEACE (Least-squares Concept Erasure), a closed-form affine transformation. It whitens the data, orthogonally projects out the target concept subspace, and unwhitens the output. It mathematically guarantees perfect linear erasure while minimizing the mean squared distance (MSE) from the original embeddings.

Strategic Advantage for ITTS (Surgical Concept Removal with Zero-Training Tax): LEACE requires no backpropagation or parameter fine-tuning and operates via an exact closed-form solution. For ITTS Text Encoders, its "least-squares minimal distortion" property ensures that implicit stereotyping (e.g., occupational gender bias) is completely neutralized in the feature space, without degrading the encoder's semantic fidelity or its ability to follow explicit user prompts.

Core Problem (Bi-Directional Gender Bias in Generation): Image captioning models suffer from two distinct yet entangled forms of gender bias: Context $\rightarrow$ Gender Bias (misclassifying gender due to spurious contextual correlations, e.g., predicting "boy" when a skateboard is present) and Gender $\rightarrow$ Context Bias (over-generating gender-stereotypical descriptors once gender is predicted).

Methodological Innovation (Synthetic Data & Post-Hoc Editing): To address both biases without retraining complex base models, the authors introduce LIBRA, a model-agnostic post-hoc editing framework. It consists of two key components: Biased Caption Synthesis (BCS)—which uses language models to automatically construct parallel pairs of heavily biased and neutral captions—and a Debiasing Caption Generator (DCG) trained to edit out spurious gender correlations while preserving image ground truth.

The Proposed Strategy (Black-Box Model-Agnostic Correction): LIBRA operates entirely at the inference stage without modifying or accessing the internals of the underlying generation backbone. By feeding candidate outputs into the DCG along with visual context, it dynamically rewrites biased wording, achieving consistent debiasing across 9 diverse model architectures.

Strategic Advantage for ITTS (Framework for Bi-Directional Acoustic Bias & Data Augmentation): LIBRA provides a conceptual blueprint for mapping bi-directional bias in ITTS—distinguishing Instruction $\rightarrow$ Acoustic Bias (e.g., neutral occupations defaulting to specific pitches) from Explicit Gender $\rightarrow$ Stereotypical Style Bias (e.g., explicit gender commands overriding acoustic diversity). Furthermore, its synthetic data generation paradigm (BCS) can be adopted to synthesize paired neutral vs. biased instruction sets for training ITTS Text Encoder debiasing modules or contrastive probes.
